plan: My private value is $26. To maximize profit, I want to win only if I can do so without paying more than my value. Since bids are sealed and values are randomly drawn, I'll aim to bid slightly above the expected midpoint of potential bids. A bid around $25-$27 seems optimal - high enough to likely win, but not so high that I risk negative profit if I pay too much.

My private value is $18. In a single-round auction with unknown opponent strategies, I want to bid strategically. Since I'll pay the third-highest bid if I win, I should bid above my value but not excessively. A reasonable approach is to bid around $22-$25 - high enough to potentially win, but not so high that I risk significant loss if my bid exceeds my true value. This allows some buffer for potential opponent bidding.

My private value is $21. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is typically to bid your true value. Since the third-highest bid determines the payment, bidding exactly $21 minimizes risk of overpaying while maximizing chance of winning. With values randomly drawn between $0-$49, other bidders might have higher or lower values. By bidding my true value, I ensure I only win if the prize is worth more to me than to others.
